column4: ~/proj/prompts/reports/SESSION-REVIEW-LEAVES-1.md item 7. Finding CONFIG-DEAD-KEYS (low, fixed in configs/): the template documented secrets.limits.max_secrets_per_user (\"Maximum number of secrets per user\", 1000) and secrets.chunking.enabled/max_chunk_size_kb/max_chunks_per_secret, none of which any code reads, so an operator relied on a per-user quota that does not exist, while the enforced secrets.limits.max_secret_size was undocumented; now the template documents max_secret_size and states the others are not enforced. New guard configs/template_keys_read_test.go:TestShippedConfigKeysAreRead (every leaf of the template, dev.yaml and test.yaml maps to a config.Config field that some non-test file selects; red on main naming exactly the three distinctive dead fields, green on the other leaves). Comment fix: session block claimed the 30m access_ttl recommendation was the default; the default is access_ttl 24h under a 12h absolute ceiling (#G37 changed only the ceiling). Tried without finding: insecure defaults in the template (TLS on, metrics token, require_mfa, require_transport_tls, ratelimits, 127.0.0.1 bind, encryption on, strict password policy, SIEM skip-verify off, membership allowlist, purge off); a fresh admin init plus encryption init and migrate gives admin validate --posture No deviations at this branch; dev variant is bannered, labelled environment local (not development, which would widen CORS) and every relaxation is a posture deviation (existing dev_template tests); dev.yaml holds no credentials; test.yaml is only a fixture and is not on any default config search path. Not covered: server/config/production.yaml, web-enabled.yaml and docs/CONFIGURATION.md carry the same dead keys (outside this session paths, see LEFTOVERS); the guard cannot see a dead key with a generic field name (Enabled)
